land.text: "Albanian territories taken from Byzantium" by Charles of Anjou, round Durrës, Berat and the coast to Butrint

predecessors.note: Infobox gives 1271 as establishment; the page says the kingdom was declared in late February 1272 and Charles signed a treaty with the Albanian nobles and the citizens of Durrës on 21 February 1272. Cliopatria lists an Albanian Principalities row only from 1375.

land.text: Durrës, which "Karl Thopia took ... from the Angevins" in 1368

successors.note: Louis of Évreux conquered Durrës in 1376, Thopia regained it in 1383, and Thopia's son Gjergj surrendered it to Venice in 1392. The Principality of Albania (Thopia) is flagged by eu-18-e as needing a dossier.

capitals.name: Durrës (Durazzo, Dyrrhachium)
capitals.note: Capital: Durazzo. Lost to the Byzantines in 1288 and regained by the Angevins in September 1304; the Serbs held it 1296-1304.

rulers.name: Philip I, Prince of Taranto
rulers.note: Charles II passed his Albanian rights to Philip in August 1294.

correction.text: Durrës, Berat, Vlorë and the coast south to Butrint, the Angevin conquests from Byzantium

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row. The page says the kingdom "ran from the Durrës region south along the coast to Butrint" at its peak and gives Berat as captured by the Byzantines in 1274, so Berat is taken as Angevin before. No area on the page.

correction.text: without Berat, captured by the Byzantines in 1274, and Butrint, which followed

keyframe_review.note: "1274: Byzantine forces captured Berat. Butrint followed later." A truce was signed in 1276. Vlorë is the researcher's reading of the coast that stayed Angevin.

correction.text: Durrës and Vlorë with Butrint and Sopot, surrendered by Nikephoros I of Epirus in March 1279

keyframe_review.note: "March 1279: Nikephoros I of Epirus surrendered Butrint and Sopot to Charles."

correction.text: the kingdom "reduced to a small area around Durrës, with Krujë and Vlorë also held"; Corfu and Butrint "remained in Angevin hands at least up to 1292", so Butrint (the Sarandë circle) stays in

keyframe_review.note: "By 1281: The Angevins were driven out of the interior" and "reduced to a small area around Durrës, with Krujë and Vlorë also held"; "Corfu and Butrint remained in Angevin hands at least up to 1292" (same page), so Butrint is kept in this shape. Berat was lost in 1274 and is not lost again in 1281. Krujë lies in the Durrës county. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: Sarandë added]

correction.text: only Vlorë and Kaninë, and Corfu and Butrint "Angevin at least until 1292", after the Byzantines took Durrës in 1288

keyframe_review.note: 1288: the Byzantines took Durrës; Kaninë, "the last Angevin holdout", fell c. 1294. Corfu is not drawn (the Ionian Islands are not in the grid's Albanian names).

correction.text: Durrës, where Angevin rule was restored in September 1304

keyframe_review.note: "1304: Serbs were expelled from Durrës, and Angevin rule was restored that September." From 1294 to 1303 the page records no Angevin territory in Albania (the Serbs under Stephen Milutin took Durrës in 1296), so no keyframe covers those years.

region.text: the Albanian territories taken from Byzantium round Durrës

ledger.note: Late February 1272: Charles of Anjou declares the Kingdom of Albania; "Charles signed a treaty with Albanian nobles and Durrës citizens on 21 February 1272". The infobox gives 1271.

Page silent on the year: Berat is Byzantine "since 1274" and "later on Butrint" fell to the same Byzantine forces; the page has Nikephoros I's troops capturing Butrint in 1278 and surrendering it to Charles in March 1279, so the 1274-1278 holder was Byzantium (the despotate-of-epirus dossier: 1278 gain from byzantine-empire). Bridged at confidence 1; counterpart changed from despotate-of-epirus [reviewer eu-18-x, 2026-11-01].

region.text: Butrint and Sopot, surrendered to Charles by Nikephoros I of Epirus

ledger.note: March 1279: Nikephoros I of Epirus surrenders Butrint and Sopot to Charles.

region.text: Berat's castle, besieged by the Angevins

ledger.note: December 1280: Angevin forces besiege the castle of Berat; in March 1281 a Byzantine relief army defeats them and captures Hugo de Sully.

March 1281: the siege of Berat fails. The page adds that the Angevins were "driven out of the interior" and reduced to Durrës, Krujë and Vlorë; no drawn land changes hands in 1281 (Berat fell in 1274; Butrint stays Angevin to at least 1292), so the event is recorded here and not as a loss.

region.text: Durrës, the capital, taken by the Byzantines

ledger.note: c. 1294: Kaninë, near Vlorë, falls; the page does not name the captor, the Byzantine Empire by the researcher's reading. In August 1294 Charles II passes his Albanian rights to Philip I.

region.text: Butrint, "Angevin at least up to 1292" (Corfu is not drawn)

ledger.note: The page says "Corfu and Butrint remained in Angevin hands at least up to 1292" and gives no later date for Butrint; the loss is bridged to 1294, the year Kaninë, the last mainland holdout, falls. The captor is the Byzantine Empire by the researcher's reading. [added after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01]

region.text: Durrës, after "Serbs were expelled" and "Angevin rule was restored that September"

ledger.note: September 1304: Angevin rule is restored at Durrës after the Serbs under Stephen Milutin (who took it in 1296) are expelled.
1368: Karl Thopia takes Durrës from the Angevins (infobox disestablishment).
1368: the Angevin kingdom ends; Louis of Évreux conquers Durrës in 1376 and Thopia regains it in 1383, but the page treats 1368 as the end.

wars.name: Angevin-Byzantine war in Albania
wars.outcome: The Byzantines took Berat (1274) and defeated the Angevin siege of its castle (December 1280 to March 1281); Nikephoros I of Epirus surrendered Butrint and Sopot in March 1279; by 1281 the Angevins were out of the interior.
wars.note: The war's name is the researcher's; a truce was signed in 1276.

wars.name: Serbian-Angevin struggle for Durrës
wars.outcome: Stephen Milutin took Durrës in 1296; the Serbs were expelled and Angevin rule was restored in September 1304.
wars.note: The Angevins held no Albanian land between 1294 and 1304.

certainty.note: A coastal lordship of cities and castles, with no frontier line on the page; the county shapes are approximate and 1294-1303 has no territory at all.

notes: Cliopatria has no row (its Albanian Principalities row starts in 1375). One page opened; it carries all dates. Gaps: the extent in 1272 (the page names Durrës, Berat and Butrint, not a boundary), Butrint between 1274 and 1279 and again after 1281 (page silent), the Corfu holding, the 1294-1303 period when the kingdom was a title only. Disagreement: infobox establishment 1271 against the 21 February 1272 treaty and the late-February declaration. The events of 1376-1392 (Louis of Évreux, Balša II, Thopia, Venice) are the successor's. Counterparts needing dossiers: principality-of-albania-thopia (flagged by eu-18-e), despotate-of-epirus exists. Wikidata id null (unreachable). Review fix (2026-11-01): Butrint (Sarandë circle) is kept through 1281-1293 and lost in 1294 (confidence 1) after the page's "at least up to 1292"; the 1281 'interior' loss is no longer an event because no drawn land changes.

sources.title: Kingdom of Albania (medieval)
sources.note: All dates: 1272 founding, 1274 Berat, 1279 Butrint, 1280-1281 siege, 1288 Durrës, 1294, 1304, 1368; rulers.
